analysis:
Both changed files are test-only: a new StreamedToolCallTests.swift (head lines 1-424) and a one-line switch case in FlintAnswerStopTests.swift (head line 128) that handles the new .toolCallDelta event. No production code, key handling, attestation, authorization or storage logic changes in the supplied units, so no concrete regression is visible here.

The tests describe a production behavior change that is outside the supplied evidence. Auto tool calls are now streamed to the coordinator as OpenAI tool_calls fragments before the frame closes, and the engine terminal is no longer the first content frame. Schema violations are refused only at frame close, so earlier fragments (name and partial arguments) can already have left the provider. Tests at lines 143-156 and 158-180 show that undeclared names are never exposed (Gemma falls back to text, Harmony fails validation unexposed) and that schema violations expose only partial deltas. This is relevant to T-007 and T-008, and to TB-002 provider-to-coordinator content framing. Provider output is untrusted, so the coordinator must tolerate partial or malformed fragments.

The test at lines 82-89 checks that the rollback env keys DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and the plain-tail seed key pass through LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys. That is an operator-controlled env passthrough on the local provider job and is not a new trust boundary.

T-008 fail-closed on encryption is not exercised here. Next review should examine the production sources not supplied: ToolStreamPreparation, NativeToolStreamRouter, MLXOpenAIService and ProviderLoop.parseStreamChunk/encodeToolCallsForHash. They should confirm that each fragment goes through the same per-chunk encryption path as other content frames, with no plaintext fallback. They should also confirm that any billing, response hashing or receipt computation covers the new fragment frames, since the hash encoding changed for partial deltas. The same pass should check the coordinator's handling of partial tool_calls.
